issue_paraphrase: When a user asks pip for information about an installed package whose metadata does not include a Metadata-Version header, pip show aborts with an ugly Python traceback ('invalid literal for int() with base 10') before printing any of the package's fields, so the command is unusable for such packages. Any distribution with incomplete or legacy metadata triggers it, and there is no way to get the package details at all.
fix_summary: pip show now treats a missing/empty Metadata-Version as an empty version tuple instead of calling int(''), which both stops the crash and falls back to printing the legacy License field rather than License-Expression. Issue #14057, fix PR #14057.

issue_paraphrase: When a requirement line contains a marker section that is not a valid environment-marker expression (for example conflicting version markers separated by semicolons), pip dies with an internal packaging exception and a raw Python traceback instead of telling the user the requirement is invalid. The failure escapes the requirement parser as an obscure error that gives no hint about which requirement line was at fault, making the command exit without a helpful message.
fix_summary: req/constructors.py now catches packaging's InvalidMarker when parsing the markers portion of a requirement line and re-raises it as InstallationError('Invalid requirement: ...'), so pip reports the offending requirement cleanly instead of crashing on an internal exception. Original report issue #6385, fixed by PR #14135.

name = Link('https://example.com/a%252Fb.whl').filename

observed_failure_at_parent: Link('https://example.com/a%252Fb.whl').filename returns 'a/b.whl': the URL path is percent-decoded once into _path and then the basename is percent-decoded a second time, so a doubly-encoded separator '%252F' collapses into a real '/'. That injects a separator into a file name derived from a URL, so the derived name no longer refers to the intended single file.

For the unit test: python -m pip install pytest 'pytest==8.4.2' 'pytest-socket==0.7.0' then cd <repo> && python -m pytest -o addopts='' -q tests/unit/test_link.py::TestLink
issue_paraphrase: When a package index or direct download URL contains a doubly percent-encoded character such as an encoded slash in the file name, pip decodes the URL twice while working out the local file name, so the stored name ends up containing a real path separator that was never part of the original file name. The result is a file name that points at a different path than the one in the URL, so downloads and build/install lookups reference the wrong file on disk.
fix_summary: Link.filename no longer percent-decodes the basename a second time (_path is already decoded once); a new PathComponent helper type and join_within_directory/as_path_component helpers ensure the derived name is used as a single path component by the download and prepare code paths. Issue #14110, fix PR #14110.
